sentences.text: Anhuilong is a genus of mamenchisaurid dinosaur found in the Hongqin Formation of Anhui province, China.
The only known fossil of Anhuilong is a single left forelimb containing a humerus, ulna, and radius.
Estimating the total length of Anhuilong is difficult due to the limited fossil evidence.
The fossilized forelimb of Anhuilong is estimated to have been about 2 meters long.
The humerus of Anhuilong measures 105 centimeters in length.
The radius is only half the length of the humerus, representing the lowest ratio known among mamenchisaurids.
The ulna is only 56% the length of the humerus, the lowest value recorded for the group.
The outer edge of the deltopectoral crest on the humerus curves backward and outward.
The additional projection on the front corner of the lower humeral edge is more robust than the one on the inner corner.
The ulna has an oval cross-section in the middle rather than a round one.
The 105-centimeter-long humerus is relatively light.
The deltopectoral crest covers 44% of the humeral shaft length and turns relatively outward.
The humeral shaft has an oval cross-section, a primitive characteristic.
The humeral shaft is twisted 25 degrees around its longitudinal axis.
The upper surface profile of the radius is rectangular, a derived characteristic.
The radius has an oval cross-section.

The discovery initially attracted little paleontological attention, but after the discoverer's death, a team from the Anhui Geological Museum examined the copy and concluded it was an unknown species.
The holotype specimen AGB 5822 was discovered in a purple sandstone layer of the Hongqin Formation dating to the early Middle Jurassic.
Anhuilong diboensis was named and described by Ren Xinxin, Huang Jiandong, and You Hailu in 2018.
The genus name Anhuilong combines the location Anhui with the Chinese word for dragon, Long.
Based on the long necks typical of Mamenchisauridae, Anhuilong likely reached about 20 meters in length and could have held its head up to 10 meters high.
Anhuilong likely weighed no more than 12 tons and had a light build.
Anhuilong is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
Phylogenetic analysis places Anhuilong as the sister taxon of Huangshanlong within the family Mamenchisauridae.
Anhuilong lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 174 to 163 million years ago, between the Aalenian and Callovian stages.
Anhuilong lived in what is now Asia.
Some researchers suggest that Anhuilong may not be distinct from Huangshanlong, viewing it as merely a copy of that taxon.
